analysis.title: "The Tail Is Wagging The Dog": 0DTE Traders Now Suppress S&P Volatility More Than Dealer Gamma
key_insights: UBS derivatives strategist Kieran Diamond's analysis of 0DTE options flow shows a shift toward tactical traders buying calls and selling puts when the market declines, and doing the opposite during rallies. UBS calls this a counter-trend delta bias.
The counter-trend flow is equivalent to buying low and selling high, which further suppresses S&P 500 swings. It resembles the stabilizing effect of positive gamma.
The growth of 0DTE counter-trend flow is now large enough that its net effect outweighs option dealer re-hedging, according to UBS.
Around 66% of overall S&P 500 option volume expires within a day, per Garrett DeSimone at OptionMetrics.
The intraday tactical shift began in 2024, with larger volumes trading on smaller moves, which helps limit S&P 500 realized volatility.
A long option-dealer gamma regime is also common in the S&P 500, driven in large part by a big institutional trader selling one-day iron condors (a put spread plus a call spread).
The pattern could reverse in an extended selloff. If 0DTE investors chase a move lower by buying puts, their flows could exacerbate the move and leave market makers managing short gamma risk.
In the technology sector, short-term trading has the opposite effect, with flows tending to exacerbate rallies and declines. This has supported successful intraday momentum strategies.

Premialab saw strong performance from semiconductor-focused intraday momentum strategies during the April-June rally. The number of live strategies for that segment in its QIS database is up 50% since the end of March 2025.
The delta-adjusted notional value in the S&P 500 option complex now easily surpasses average daily volume in E-Mini futures, so the options tail at times wags the stock dog.

JPMorgan derivatives strategists moved from an open-interest proxy for S&P 500 gamma positioning to a flow-based approach. It uses Cboe data showing whether clients bought or sold each option transaction.

sector_views.rationale: Short-term trading in tech tends to amplify intraday rallies and declines, the opposite of the dampening seen in the S&P 500 overall. This is a flow observation, not a directional view.

risk_factors: The counter-trend 0DTE pattern could reverse in a period of higher volatility or an extended selloff.
If 0DTE traders buy puts into declines, their flows could exacerbate the move and leave market makers short gamma.
Positioning models based on open interest may misstate dealer gamma.
